title: The invisible side of design engineering
brief: Jakub Krehel's essay on the invisible side of design engineering — the craft that doesn't show up in the final pixels. A thoughtful read for design-minded engineers.
details: An essay by Jakub (jakub.kr, author of the Interfaces design-engineering magazine) on what design engineering actually looks like day to day. His argument: social media makes the discipline look like animated eye-candy components, but the invisible half — accessibility, responsiveness, performance, edge cases that only appear when real people use the product — is just as important, if not more. Concrete examples: an afternoon fixing an accessibility issue few will notice, obsessing over landing-page load time. The throughline is that a great experience is mostly invisible, and the job is making sure the experience is great for all kinds of people, not just building what photographs well. A good corrective read for anyone whose sense of the craft comes from Twitter demos.
